q: On what basis are biotic and abiotic resources classified?
o: On the basis of status of development
e: On the basis of origin, resources are classified into biotic (obtained from the biosphere) and abiotic (composed of non-living things).

q: Which of the following is an example of a biotic resource?
e: Livestock, human beings, flora, and fauna are biotic resources obtained from the biosphere and have life.

q: What type of resources are solar energy and wind energy?
e: Solar and wind energy are renewable (replenishable) resources that can be renewed by physical or mechanical processes.

q: Which category of resources do fossil fuels (coal, petroleum) belong to?
e: Fossil fuels are non-renewable resources because they take millions of years to form and get exhausted with use.

q: On the basis of ownership, what type of resources are public parks, burial grounds, and village ponds?
e: These resources are accessible to all members of the community and are therefore called community owned resources.

q: Who regulates open oceanic resources beyond 200 nautical miles of the Exclusive Economic Zone?
e: Oceanic resources beyond 200 nautical miles belong to the open ocean and no individual country can utilise them without the concurrence of international institutions.

q: In which city was the first International Earth Summit held in June 1992?
e: In June 1992, more than 100 heads of states met in Rio de Janeiro in Brazil for the first International Earth Summit.

q: In which summit was "Agenda 21" adopted?
e: Agenda 21 was adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit to achieve global sustainable development in the 21st century.

q: According to the National Forest Policy (1952), what percentage of India’s geographical area is desired under forest cover?
e: According to the National Forest Policy (1952), 33 per cent of geographical area is desired under forests to maintain ecological balance.

q: What is the approximate total geographical area of India?
e: Total geographical area of India is 3.28 million sq km, though land use data is available only for 93 per cent of it.

q: Approximately what percentage of India’s land area is under plains?
e: About 43 per cent of India’s land area is plain, 30 per cent is mountains, and about 27 per cent is the plateau region.

q: Which is the most widely spread and important soil in India?
e: Alluvial soil is the most widely spread and important soil in India, covering the entire northern plains.

q: What is the other common name of black soil?
e: Black soil is also known as regur soil and black cotton soil.

q: Black soil is considered ideal for growing which main crop?
e: Black soil is ideal for growing cotton and is also known as black cotton soil.

q: By what name is old alluvial soil known?
e: According to age, old alluvial soil is known as Bangar (with higher concentration of kanker nodules) and new alluvial as Khadar.

q: What is new alluvial soil called?
e: New alluvial soil is called Khadar; it has more fine particles and is more fertile than the Bangar.

q: The word "Laterite" has been derived from which language’s word "later" meaning brick?
e: Laterite has been derived from the Latin word "later" which means brick.

q: Red soil develops a reddish colour mainly due to diffusion of which element?
e: Red soil develops a reddish colour due to diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks; it looks yellow when it occurs in a hydrated form.

q: Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are more suitable for which crop?
e: Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are more suitable for crops like cashew nut.

q: What is the denudation of the soil cover and subsequent washing down described as?
e: The denudation of the soil cover and subsequent washing down is described as soil erosion.

q: What are the bad lands created by deep gullies in the Chambal basin locally called?
e: In the Chambal basin, bad lands caused by gully erosion are locally called ravines.

q: What is ploughing along the contour lines on slopes called?
e: Ploughing along the contour lines can decelerate the flow of water down the slopes; this is called contour ploughing.

q: Growing strips of grass between crops to break up the force of the wind is called:
e: Large fields are divided into strips and strips of grass are left to grow between the crops to break wind force; this is known as strip cropping.

q: In which Indian state is arid soil mainly found?
e: Arid soils range from red to brown, are sandy and saline, and are typically found in western Rajasthan.

q: Land left without cultivation for one or less than one agricultural year is called:
e: Land left without cultivation for one or less than one agricultural year is known as current fallow.

q: In which part of India does terrace cultivation mainly restrict soil erosion?
e: Steps cut out on slopes making terraces restrict erosion; Western and Central Himalayas have well developed terrace farming.

q: Planting lines of trees to create shelter and stabilise sand dunes is called:
e: Planting lines of trees to create shelter works in a similar way; rows of such trees are called shelter belts, which stabilise sand dunes.

q: "There is enough for everybody’s need and not for any body’s greed." Who said these words?
e: Mahatma Gandhi placed the greedy and selfish individuals as the root cause of resource depletion with this famous statement.

q: Which chemical constituents are found in adequate proportion in alluvial soil?
e: Mostly alluvial soils contain adequate proportion of potash, phosphoric acid and lime, ideal for sugarcane, paddy and wheat.

q: Black soil is mainly found in which region of India?
e: Black soil is typical of the Deccan trap (Basalt) region spread over northwest Deccan plateau covering Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Malwa, MP and Chhattisgarh.

q: Which one of the following is the main cause of land degradation in Punjab? [JAC PYQ]
e: In Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, over irrigation is responsible for land degradation due to water logging leading to increase in salinity and alkalinity.

q: In which one of the following states is terrace cultivation practised? [JAC PYQ]
e: Terrace cultivation is practised in mountainous states like Uttarakhand (Western and Central Himalayas) to control soil erosion.

q: In which of the following states is black soil predominantly found? [JAC PYQ]
e: Black soil is predominantly found in Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Malwa, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh plateau.

q: Which type of resource is iron ore? [JAC PYQ]
e: Iron ore and other minerals are non-renewable resources as they take millions of years in their formation and cannot be renewed quickly.

q: Under which of the following types of resource can tidal energy be put? [JAC PYQ]
e: Tidal energy, along with solar and wind energy, is a replenishable (renewable) resource.

q: What is the main cause of land degradation in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha?
e: In states like Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha, deforestation due to mining has caused severe land degradation.

q: What is one of the main reasons for land degradation in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra?
e: In states like Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, overgrazing is one of the main reasons for land degradation.

q: Who wrote the book "Small is Beautiful" reiterating Gandhian philosophy on resource conservation?
e: In 1974, Gandhian philosophy was once again presented by Schumacher in his book "Small is Beautiful".

q: Under what title was the Brundtland Commission Report (1987) subsequently published as a book?
e: The Brundtland Commission Report (1987) introduced Sustainable Development, subsequently published in a book entitled "Our Common Future".

q: Which organisation advocated resource conservation for the first time in a systematic way at the international level in 1968?
e: At the international level, the Club of Rome advocated resource conservation for the first time in a more systematic way in 1968.

q: Roughly what percentage of total area is Net Sown Area in Punjab and Haryana?
e: Net sown area is over 80 per cent of the total area in Punjab and Haryana and less than 10 per cent in Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur and Andaman & Nicobar.

q: What is land left uncultivated for more than 5 agricultural years called?
e: Land left uncultivated for more than 5 agricultural years is categorised as culturable waste land.

q: Land left uncultivated for 1 to 5 agricultural years is classified under which category?
e: Land left uncultivated for the past 1 to 5 agricultural years is known as fallow other than current fallow.

q: Which soil has high moisture-holding capacity, is poor in phosphoric contents, and develops deep cracks during hot weather?
e: Black soil is made of extremely fine clayey material, retains moisture, is poor in phosphoric contents, and develops deep cracks in hot weather helping proper aeration.

q: Laterite soil is mainly a result of which process?
o: Intense leaching due to heavy rain
e: Laterite soil develops under tropical and subtropical climate with alternate wet and dry season, and is the result of intense leaching due to heavy rain.

q: What are alluvial plains in the piedmont plains of the Himalayas commonly called?
e: Alluvial soils are common in piedmont plains such as Duars, Chos and Terai.

q: When water flows as a sheet over large areas down a slope washing away the top soil, it is known as:
e: Water flowing as a sheet over large areas down a slope and washing away topsoil is called sheet erosion.

q: In arid soil, the Kankar layer formations in the lower horizons are due to increasing content of:
e: In arid soil, the lower horizons are occupied by Kankar because of the increasing calcium content downwards, which restricts the infiltration of water.

q: Which region of India provides an example of huge "potential resources" of wind and solar energy?
e: The western parts of India particularly Rajasthan and Gujarat have enormous potential for the development of wind and solar energy.

q: Water (compound of hydrogen and oxygen) is cited as an example of which resource category because we lack technical know-how to use its gases as energy?
e: Materials in the environment which have the potential to satisfy human needs but humans do not have the appropriate technology to access them (like H2 and O2 from water) are included among Stock.

q: River water and forests, which can be put into use with existing technical know-how but whose use has not been started fully, are subsets of Stock known as:
e: Reserves are the subset of stock which can be put into use with existing technical know-how, such as river water for hydroelectricity or forests.

q: In the eastern coastal plains, alluvial soil is particularly found in the deltas of which rivers?
e: Alluvial soil is also found in the eastern coastal plains particularly in the deltas of the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri rivers.

q: How does grinding of limestone for cement industry and calcite/soapstone for ceramic industry cause land degradation?
o: Huge dust in atmosphere retarding water infiltration into soil
e: Mineral processing generates huge quantity of dust in the atmosphere, which retards the process of infiltration of water into the soil after it settles down on the land.

q: What is the general chemical nature of laterite soil in terms of pH?
e: Laterite soil is mostly deep to very deep, acidic (pH < 6.0), and generally deficient in plant nutrients.

q: What is the nature of forest soil in the snow-covered areas of the Himalayas?
e: In the snow-covered areas of Himalayas, forest soils experience denudation and are acidic with low humus content.

q: In India, which soil is widely found in Odisha, Chhattisgarh, southern parts of middle Ganga plain and piedmont zone of Western Ghats?
e: Yellow and red soils are found in parts of Odisha, Chhattisgarh, southern parts of the middle Ganga plain and along the piedmont zone of the Western Ghats.

q: Land use data for which parts of India has mostly not been done?
o: Most North-east states except Assam and POK/China occupied parts of J&K
e: Land use reporting for most north-east states except Assam has not been done fully, and areas of J&K occupied by Pakistan and China have also not been surveyed.

q: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area is known as:
e: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area is known as gross cropped area.

q: Which global ecological crisis has arisen due to the indiscriminate exploitation of resources?
e: Indiscriminate exploitation of resources has led to global ecological crises such as global warming, ozone layer depletion, environmental pollution and land degradation.

q: Which is the first step of resource planning in India?
o: Matching development plans with national plans
Identification and inventory of resources across the regions of the country
e: The first step of resource planning involves identification and inventory of resources across regions through surveying, mapping and qualitative/quantitative estimation.

q: Which pair of Indian states shares "mining" as the primary cause of severe land degradation?
e: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, MP and Odisha suffer severe land degradation due to mining and deforestation, whereas Punjab-Haryana face over-irrigation and Gujarat-Rajasthan face overgrazing.

q: A farmer’s field on an old flood terrace contains high concentration of Kanker nodules. Which soil type is this?
e: Old alluvial soil (Bangar) has higher concentration of kanker nodules compared to newer, finer and more fertile Khadar soil.

q: If a region experiences dry climate, high temperature, and rapid evaporation, which soil is most likely formed there?
e: Due to dry climate and high temperature, evaporation is faster and the soil lacks humus and moisture, resulting in arid soil.

q: Why is solar energy in Rajasthan classified as a "Potential resource" rather than "Stock"?
o: Because no technology exists at all to use it
Because it is useless for humans
Because it is found in the region and technology exists, yet it has not been utilised extensively
e: Potential resources are those found in a region but have not been fully utilised yet, such as wind and solar energy in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

q: What is the correct logical sequence of the three steps involved in resource planning in India?
o: Set up technology → Survey & inventory → Match national plan
Identification & inventory → Evolving planning structure with technology & institutions → Matching with national development plans
e: The sequence is: (1) identification and inventory, (2) evolving planning structure with appropriate technology, skill and institutions, and (3) matching plans with overall national development plans.

q: Identify the correctly matched pair of Indian region and its specific resource endowment/deficit:
o: Arunachal Pradesh — rich in minerals but lacks water
Ladakh — rich in cultural heritage but deficient in water, infrastructure and vital minerals
Rajasthan — rich in water but lacks solar energy
Jharkhand — completely devoid of minerals and coal
e: The cold desert of Ladakh is relatively isolated; it has a very rich cultural heritage but is deficient in water, infrastructure and some vital minerals.

q: What is one major objective of Agenda 21?
o: Allow developed nations to increase coal output
Every local government should draw its own local Agenda 21
Reduce EEZ from 200 to 12 nautical miles
e: One major objective of Agenda 21 is that every local government should draw its own local Agenda 21 to combat environmental damage, poverty and disease through global cooperation.

q: Why does black soil exhibit a "self-aeration" property during hot weather?
o: Presence of clayey material causing deep cracks during hot weather
e: Black soil develops deep cracks during hot weather due to its clayey texture, which helps in proper aeration of the soil.

q: Why is forest soil found in the lower parts of valleys particularly fertile?
o: Presence of river terraces and alluvial fans
e: In the lower parts of the valleys particularly on the river terraces and alluvial fans, forest soils are fertile.

q: Why does the pattern of Net Sown Area vary greatly across Indian states (over 80% in Punjab/Haryana vs below 10% in Arunachal/Mizoram)?
o: Physical factors (topography, climate, soil types) as well as human factors
e: Land use is determined by physical factors such as topography, climate and soil types as well as human factors like population density and technological capability.

q: Laterite soil in hilly areas of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu becomes useful for growing tea and coffee especially after:
e: After adopting appropriate soil conservation techniques particularly in the hilly areas of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, laterite soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee.

q: A farmer over-irrigates his land leading to waterlogging and soil salinity. This scenario is most characteristic of which Indian region?
o: Western Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana
e: In Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, over-irrigation leads to water logging and increases soil salinity and alkalinity.

q: An entrepreneur setting up a cotton ginning unit would most likely locate near which soil belt?
o: Black soil of Saurashtra and Malwa
e: Black (regur) soil covering Maharashtra, Saurashtra and Malwa is ideal for cotton cultivation.

q: Although forest cover rose marginally since 1960-61, it remains far below the 33% mark set by the National Forest Policy (1952). Why is this 33% threshold essential?
o: For maintaining ecological balance and supporting livelihood of millions living on forest fringes
e: 33 per cent forest cover was considered essential for maintenance of ecological balance and the livelihood of millions of people who live on the fringes of these forests.

q: Which conservation method is most effective in checking the shifting of sand dunes in western Rajasthan?
e: Shelter belts (rows of trees) break wind speed and have contributed significantly to the stabilisation of sand dunes in western India.

q: Which group correctly lists the major factors responsible for soil formation?
o: Relief, parent rock, climate, vegetation and time
e: Relief, parent rock or bed rock, climate, vegetation and other forms of life and time are important factors in the formation of soil.

q: Which type of land is categorised under "Barren and waste land"?
e: Barren and waste land includes rocky, arid and desert areas, distinct from land put to non-agricultural uses like settlements, roads, railways and industries.

q: What primarily attracted foreign invaders/colonisers to India and other colonies?
o: Rich resources of colonies combined with higher level of technological development of colonising countries
e: Rich resources in colonies were the main attractions for foreign invaders, exploited through the higher level of technological development of the colonising countries.

q: Which of the following is the odd one out in terms of ownership classification of resources?
o: Land allotted to farmers by government
Plantations, pasture lands and private wells
e: The first three are examples of individual resources, whereas public picnic spots and playgrounds are community owned resources.

q: All minerals, water resources, forests, wildlife within political boundaries and oceanic area up to 12 nautical miles (22.2 km) from the coast are classified as:
e: Technically all resources belong to the nation; all resources within political boundaries and oceanic area up to 12 nautical miles (territorial water) are National Resources.

q: How can land degradation caused by industrial effluents be effectively controlled?
o: Proper discharge and disposal of industrial effluents and wastes after treatment
e: Proper discharge and disposal of industrial effluents and wastes after treatment can reduce land and water degradation in industrial and suburban areas.

q: Why is the assumption "Resources are free gifts of nature" considered flawed in modern geography?
o: Because resources are a function of human activities and humans themselves are essential components of resources
e: Resources are not free gifts of nature; they are a function of human activities. Human beings interact with nature through technology and institutions to transform materials into resources.

q: How does the high fertility of alluvial soil (supporting sugarcane, paddy, wheat, pulses) impact the regions where it occurs?
o: Regions of alluvial soils are intensively cultivated and densely populated
e: Due to its high fertility, regions of alluvial soils are intensively cultivated and densely populated.

q: What happens if a field on a slope is ploughed up and down (along the slope) rather than along contour lines?
o: Channels form for the quick flow of water leading to soil erosion
e: Defective methods of farming such as ploughing in a wrong way (up and down the slope) form channels for the quick flow of water leading to soil erosion.

q: How has arid soil in western Rajasthan been made cultivable after proper irrigation became available?
o: After proper irrigation these soils have become cultivable as has been in the case of western Rajasthan
e: Although arid soil is sandy and saline, after proper irrigation these soils have become cultivable as seen in the case of western Rajasthan.

q: According to NCERT estimates, roughly how much degraded land was there in India (comprising forest degraded, water eroded, wind eroded, and saline/alkaline lands)?
e: India has about 130 million hectares of degraded land, of which roughly 28% is forest degraded area, 56% is water eroded, and the rest is affected by saline/alkaline deposits and wind erosion.

q: What is a major challenge resulting from the decrease in land under permanent pastures in India?
o: Difficult to feed the huge cattle population on the remaining pasture land
e: The land under permanent pasture has decreased, making it difficult to feed India’s huge cattle population on the remaining pasture land.

q: How do alkaline alluvial soils in the drier areas behave with respect to fertility?
o: They can become productive after proper treatment and irrigation
e: Alluvial soils in drier areas are more alkaline and can be productive after proper treatment and irrigation.

q: Which soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan plateau?
e: Red soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan plateau.

q: Choose the correct statement regarding resource availability and regional economic development:
o: Mere availability of resources guarantees development
Availability of resources is necessary, but mere availability without corresponding changes in technology and institutions may hinder development
e: Mere availability of resources in the absence of corresponding changes in technology and institutions may hinder development; many resource-rich regions are economically backward while some resource-poor regions are well developed.

q:

Reason (R): There is enormous diversity in the availability of resources across regions in India—some regions are rich in certain resources while deficient in others.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Regions like Jharkhand are rich in minerals while Rajasthan lacks water but has solar/wind energy; hence balanced resource planning is vital.

o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Black soil’s fine clayey texture and high moisture-retention capacity directly make it ideal for growing cotton.

Reason (R): Khadar is old alluvial soil with a very high concentration of kanker nodules.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

q:
Assertion (A): Resources are merely free gifts of nature.
Reason (R): Resources are a function of human activities because human beings transform materials into resources using technology.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false because resources are not free gifts of nature; Reason (R) is true as human beings transform materials into resources.

q:
Assertion (A): Over-irrigation is the main cause of land degradation in Punjab and Haryana.
Reason (R): Over-irrigation causes water logging, which increases salinity and alkalinity in the soil.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Over-irrigation in Punjab and Haryana causes water logging, leading to increased salinity and alkalinity; R correctly explains A.

q:
Assertion (A): Laterite soil is the result of intense leaching due to heavy rain in tropical and subtropical climates.
Reason (R): This soil always has uniformly high humus content across all terrains and climates.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is true, while Reason (R) is false because laterite soil is humus poor under sparse vegetation and semi-arid environments.

q:
Assertion (A): The first International Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil in June 1992.
Reason (R): The summit was convened for addressing urgent problems of environmental protection and socio-economic development at the global level.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) accurately explains why the 1992 Rio Earth Summit was convened.

q:
Assertion (A): The Kankar layer in the lower horizons of arid soil restricts water infiltration.
Reason (R): In arid soils, calcium content increases downwards leading to the formation of Kankar layers.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Increasing calcium content downwards forms Kankar layers in arid soil, which directly restricts water infiltration.

q:
Assertion (A): In India, 33 per cent of geographical area is desired under forest cover.
Reason (R): The total geographical area of India is 3.28 million sq km.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are individually true facts, but India’s total area being 3.28 million sq km is not the reason for the 33% forest target.

q:
Assertion (A): Terrace cultivation in the Western and Central Himalayas helps restrict soil erosion.
Reason (R): Cutting steps on slopes slows down the flow of water down the slope and prevents topsoil loss.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Cutting terraces on slopes slows down runoff and retains soil; R correctly explains A.

q:
Assertion (A): Red soil looks yellow when it occurs in a hydrated form.
Reason (R): Red soil is formed primarily from the basaltic lava flows of the Deccan trap.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is true, while Reason (R) is false because red soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks, whereas basaltic lava flows formed black soil.

q:
Assertion (A): Mining has played a major role in land degradation in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.
Reason (R): Mining sites are abandoned after excavation work is complete leaving deep scars and traces of overburdening.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Abandoned mining sites leaving deep scars and overburdening alongside deforestation explain severe land degradation in these states.

q:
Assertion (A): At the international level, the Club of Rome advocated resource conservation systematically for the first time in 1968.
Reason (R): About 43 per cent of India’s land area is under plains.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true independently, but India’s plain percentage does not explain the 1968 Club of Rome initiative.

q:
Assertion (A): Growing strips of grass between crops in large fields is called shelter belts.
Reason (R): Strips of grass break up the force of the wind and reduce wind erosion.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false because growing strips of grass between crops is called "strip cropping" (not shelter belts); Reason (R) is true.

q:
Assertion (A): Sustainable development means development should take place without damaging the environment.
Reason (R): Development in the present should not compromise with the needs of the future generations.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Environmental protection and safeguarding future generations’ needs together define and explain sustainable economic development.

q:
Assertion (A): Water (H2O) is treated as an example of "Stock" in the context of energy sources.
Reason (R): Water is a compound of two inflammable gases, hydrogen and oxygen, which can be a rich source of energy, but we do not have the required technical know-how to use them for this purpose.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Because we lack the required technical know-how to harness H2 and O2 from water cheaply at scale, water illustrates Stock; R explains A.

q:
Assertion (A): In the Chambal basin, deep gullies form because black soil holds excessive moisture.
Reason (R): Running water cutting through clayey soils and making deep channels is called gully erosion.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false (ravines in Chambal are due to running water cutting deep gullies, not moisture holding of black soil); Reason (R) accurately defines gully erosion.

q:
Assertion (A): Dust emission from grinding limestone in the cement industry contributes to land degradation.
Reason (R): About 27 per cent of India’s land area is plateau region possessing rich reserves of minerals and fossil fuels.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true independently, but India’s 27% plateau area does not explain how cement dust retards water infiltration.

q:
Assertion (A): Oceanic resources up to 12 nautical miles from the coast belong to the nation as National Resources.
Reason (R): A country’s government has legal powers to acquire even private property for public good.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true aspects of National Resources, yet domestic eminent domain does not explain the 12 nautical mile territorial limit.

q:
Assertion (A): India’s forest area has been reduced to half since the National Forest Policy of 1952.
Reason (R): Actually, the share of forest area increased marginally from 18.11% in 1960-61 to about 23.3% in 2014-15, though still below the desired 33%.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false because reported forest area did not halve; Reason (R) accurately reflects the marginal rise from 18.11% to 23.3%.

q:
Read the passage: "An equitable distribution of resources has become essential for a sustained quality of life and global peace. If the present trend of resource depletion by a few individuals and countries continues, the future of our planet is in danger. Therefore, resource planning is essential for sustainable existence of all forms of life. Sustainable existence is a component of sustainable development."

According to the passage, what is essential for a sustained quality of life and global peace?
o: Concentration of resources in a few countries
e: The passage explicitly states that an equitable distribution of resources is essential for a sustained quality of life and global peace.

q: Based on the same passage, what is essential for the sustainable existence of all forms of life?
e: The passage states that resource planning is essential for sustainable existence of all forms of life.

q: Which landmark report in 1987 introduced the concept of "Sustainable Development" mentioned in the passage?
e: The Brundtland Commission Report (1987) introduced the concept of Sustainable Development and advocated resource conservation.

q: Indiscriminate accumulation of resources in a few hands has divided society into which two segments?
o: Haves and have nots (rich and poor)
e: Accumulation of resources in few hands divided the society into two segments i.e. haves and have nots or rich and poor.

q: Which summit adopted Agenda 21 to operationalise sustainable development in line with the passage above?
e: The 1992 Rio Earth Summit adopted Agenda 21 for achieving global sustainable development.

q:
Read the passage: "These soils are black in colour and are also known as regur soils. Climatic condition along with the parent rock material are the important factors for the formation of black soil. This type of soil is typical of the Deccan trap (Basalt) region spread over northwest Deccan plateau and is made up of lava flows. They are made up of extremely fine i.e. clayey material. They are well-known for their capacity to hold moisture."

Which parent rock material played a major role in forming this soil?
e: As stated in the passage, black soil is typical of the Deccan trap (Basalt) region and is made up of lava flows.

q: Which nutrients are rich in black soil, and which constituent is generally poor in it?
o: Rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash and lime; poor in phosphoric contents
Rich only in nitrogen; poor in iron
e: Black soil is rich in soil nutrients such as calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash and lime, while generally poor in phosphoric contents.

q: Why should black soil be tilled immediately after the first shower or during the pre-monsoon period?
o: Because it washes into the sea
Because it becomes sticky when wet and difficult to work on unless tilled early
e: Black soils are sticky when wet and difficult to work on unless tilled immediately after the first shower or during the pre-monsoon period.

q: Besides Maharashtra, Malwa and Chhattisgarh plateaus, along which river valleys does black soil extend in the south-east direction?
e: Black soil covers the plateaus of Maharashtra, Saurashtra, Malwa, MP and Chhattisgarh and extends south-east along the Godavari and the Krishna valleys.

q: Which other name is also used for the soil described in the passage above?
e: Black soil is also known as regur soil and black cotton soil due to its suitability for cotton.

q:
Consider the following statements about alluvial soil:
I. Alluvial soil contains adequate potash, phosphoric acid and lime.
II. Bangar has more fine particles than Khadar.
III. Deltas of Mahanadi and Godavari in the eastern coast are made of alluvial soil.
Which statements are correct?
e: Statements I and III are correct. Statement II is false because Khadar has more fine particles and is more fertile than Bangar.

q: Which one of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Chambal basin — Eroded by shelter belts
Laterite — Heavy rain and intense leaching
e: The Chambal basin is famous for ravines caused by gully erosion, whereas shelter belts are a conservation measure against wind erosion.

q:
Identify the correctly matched state–degradation cause pairs:
1. Odisha — Mining
2. Rajasthan — Overgrazing
3. Haryana — Over-irrigation
4. Maharashtra — Glacial erosion
e: Odisha (mining), Rajasthan (overgrazing), and Haryana (over-irrigation) are correct; Maharashtra faces overgrazing rather than glacial/desert erosion.

q:
Match the fallow/waste land category with its uncultivated duration:
A. Current fallow — 1. More than 5 agricultural years
B. Other than current fallow — 2. 1 or less agricultural year
C. Culturable waste land — 3. 1 to 5 agricultural years
e: Current fallow = ≤ 1 agricultural year; Other than current fallow = 1 to 5 years; Culturable waste land = > 5 agricultural years.

q: Which statement accurately reflects NCERT’s data on the shares of India’s degraded land (~130 million hectares)?
o: Water eroded area (56%) is the largest share, followed by forest degraded area (28%)
Wind eroded area (56%) is the largest share
e: Of India’s ~130 million hectares of degraded land, roughly 56% is water eroded, 28% is forest degraded, 10% wind eroded, and 6% saline/alkaline.

q:
Arrange the following global milestones in resource conservation chronologically (earliest to latest):
1. Brundtland Commission Report
2. Club of Rome advocacy
3. Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit
4. E.F. Schumacher’s "Small is Beautiful"
e: Club of Rome (1968) → Small is Beautiful (1974) → Brundtland Report (1987) → Rio Earth Summit (1992).

q: How does the particle size of alluvial soil change from the upper reaches of a river valley towards the coastal plains?
o: Particles become finer towards the mountains
Particles appear somewhat bigger towards upper reaches/piedmont and become finer towards river mouths
e: Soil components appear somewhat bigger in size in the upper reaches of the river valley (near the place of the break of slope) and become finer towards the river mouths.

q:
Which statements about Laterite soil are true?
I. Its pH is generally less than 6.0 (acidic).
II. Under deciduous and evergreen forests it is humus rich, but under sparse vegetation and semi-arid climate it is humus poor.
III. It is richer in potash and calcium than alluvial deltas.
e: Statements I and II are true per NCERT. Statement III is false because intense leaching leaves laterite soils generally deficient in plant nutrients.

q: What is the exact legal distinction between the 12 nautical mile and 200 nautical mile oceanic zones?
o: Up to 12 nm is international; up to 200 nm is individual
Up to 12 nm (22.2 km) are national resources; beyond 200 nm of EEZ are international resources
Both zones belong only to state governments
Anyone can mine up to 200 nm without consent
e: Oceanic area up to 12 nautical miles (22.2 km) belongs to the nation, whereas oceanic resources beyond 200 nautical miles of the EEZ belong to open ocean regulated by international institutions.

q:
Examine the statements on resource ownership:
1. Private grazing land or wells owned by individuals are individual resources.
2. Village grazing grounds and public ponds are community owned resources.
3. Minerals and forests within political boundaries are national resources.
Which are correct?
e: All three examples strictly match NCERT’s classification of resources on the basis of ownership.

q: What distinguishes "Reserves" from "Developed resources" in resource classification?
o: Developed resources are surveyed and currently utilised, whereas reserves have usable technology yet their full utilisation is saved for future requirements
e: Developed resources are surveyed with quality determined for current utilisation; reserves have existing know-how available, yet their use is kept limited or postponed for future needs.

q: If a state’s land-use profile shows Net Sown Area under 10% and dense hilly forests covering large parts, which state is it most likely to be?
e: Net sown area is less than 10% in Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur and Andaman & Nicobar Islands, contrasting with over 80% in Punjab and Haryana.

q: Which of the following is NOT a human-induced cause of land degradation?
o: Natural weathering of high mountain peaks by glaciers
e: Deforestation, overgrazing, mining, quarrying and over-irrigation are human activities accelerating land degradation.

q: In which region is stabilisation of sand dunes via thorny bushes and shelter belts the primary land-conservation concern rather than terrace farming?
o: Arid and semi-arid desert regions of Western India
e: Stabilisation of sand dunes by growing thorny bushes and planting shelter belts are key methods to check land degradation in arid areas of western India.

q:
Match the type of soil erosion with its mechanism:
1. Gully erosion — A. Water flows as a sheet washing away top soil
2. Sheet erosion — B. Running water cuts deep channels in clayey soil
3. Wind erosion — C. Wind blows loose soil off flat or sloping land
e: Gully erosion cuts deep channels (1-B); sheet erosion washes topsoil as a sheet (2-A); wind erosion blows loose soil off land (3-C).

q: What is the descending order (largest to smallest share) of India’s major relief features?
e: India has about 43% plains, 30% mountains (ensuring perennial flow of rivers and tourism/ecology), and about 27% plateau region.

q: Which statement correctly matches India’s relief feature with its primary resource role as described in NCERT?
o: Plains (43%) — Rich reserves of minerals and fossil fuels
Mountains (30%) — Ensure perennial flow of some rivers and provide facilities for tourism & ecological aspects
Plateaus (27%) — Ideal exclusively for intensive paddy farming
e: Plains (43%) facilitate agriculture/industry; Mountains (30%) ensure perennial river flow and tourism/ecology; Plateaus (27%) possess rich reserves of minerals, fossil fuels and forests.

q: Which statement is INCORRECT regarding variations in Forest soil across mountain terrains?
o: They are loamy and silty in valley sides
They are coarse grained in the upper slopes
In snow-covered Himalayan areas they have extremely high humus content and are alkaline
Soil texture varies according to mountain environment
e: In snow-covered areas of the Himalayas, forest soils experience denudation and are acidic with LOW humus content (not high/alkaline).

q: According to NCERT’s triangular interactive diagram, what three elements interact with human beings to accelerate economic development?
e: Human beings interact with nature through technology and create institutions to accelerate their economic development.

q:
Which combination identifies the true properties of alluvial soil?
1. Consists of various proportions of sand, silt and clay
2. Exclusively acidic with pH < 5.0
3. Ideal for sugarcane, paddy, wheat and pulse crops
4. Adequate potash, phosphoric acid and lime
e: Alluvial soil has varied proportions of sand, silt and clay, is ideal for sugarcane, paddy, wheat and pulses, and contains adequate potash, phosphoric acid and lime.

q: Which of the following is NOT recommended as a method to control land degradation?
o: Afforestation and proper management of grazing
Stabilisation of sand dunes by growing thorny bushes
Abandoning deep mining trenches open to erosion
Proper management of waste lands and control of mining activities
e: Leaving deep mining trenches open causes severe land degradation; all other options are genuine conservation measures.

q: Which two major agreements/documents were endorsed at the Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit 1992?
o: Declaration on Global Climatic Change and Biological Diversity & Global Forest Principles / Agenda 21
e: Leaders signed the Declaration on Global Climatic Change and Biological Diversity, endorsed global Forest Principles and adopted Agenda 21.

q: Plot X has been left uncultivated for 4 agricultural years and Plot Y for 6 agricultural years. How are Plot X and Plot Y classified in land-use statistics?
o: X: Current fallow; Y: Net sown area
X: Fallow other than current fallow; Y: Culturable waste land
X: Culturable waste land; Y: Current fallow
e: Uncultivated for 1–5 agricultural years = Fallow other than current fallow (X); uncultivated for >5 years = Culturable waste land (Y).

q: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding resource conservation:
o: Gandhiji placed the mass production approach below production by the masses
Irrational consumption of resources leads to socio-economic and environmental problems
Schumacher presented Gandhian philosophy in "Small is Beautiful" in 1974
Unlimited greed-driven industrialisation is the sole recognised path to sustainable development
e: Gandhiji opposed greedy, exploitative modern technology and advocated production by the masses over mass production; greed-driven exploitation is unsustainable.

q: Which statement accurately describes Jharkhand’s resource and land-use paradox?
o: Jharkhand is rich in minerals and coal deposits, yet faces challenges of economic lag and mining-induced land degradation
Jharkhand has only alluvial soil and 85% net sown area
Mining is banned in Jharkhand since 1952
e: NCERT notes that Jharkhand, MP and Chhattisgarh are rich in minerals and coal deposits, yet suffer severe land degradation due to mining and deforestation.

q: Choose the statement that correctly differentiates Black, Red and Laterite soils:
o: Black soil forms from basaltic lava; Red soil on crystalline igneous rocks; Laterite due to intense leaching
Black soil forms from leaching; Laterite from lava
All three occur only in Thar desert
e: Their origins differ sharply: Black soil from Deccan lava flows, Red soil on crystalline igneous rocks, and Laterite from intense leaching.

q: Which pair lists ONLY natural agents of soil erosion rather than defective human practices?
e: Natural forces like wind, glacier and water lead to soil erosion, whereas deforestation, over-grazing, construction and mining are human activities.

q: Land use data in India is available for only 93% of its 3.28 million sq km total area mainly because:
o: The rest is submerged under ocean
Survey of most North-East states except Assam and parts of J&K occupied by Pakistan and China has not been done
e: Land use reporting for most north-east states except Assam has not been done fully, and some areas of Jammu and Kashmir occupied by Pakistan and China have also not been surveyed.

q: What notable economic activity is associated with high salt content in arid soils at some places?
o: Obtaining common salt by evaporating the water
e: In some areas, the salt content in arid soil is very high and common salt is obtained by evaporating the water.

q: What framework of action did Agenda 21 establish at the 1992 Rio Summit to tackle environmental damage, poverty and disease?
o: Global co-operation on common interests, mutual needs and shared responsibilities
Closing all industries in developing countries
e: Agenda 21 aims at combating environmental damage, poverty and disease through global co-operation on common interests, mutual needs and shared responsibilities.
